Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).

Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.

Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

reasons: Directionally correct: the edit converts the bare 'are the property of Company' statement into an express, irrevocable assignment of all right, title and interest (including IP) in the Works to us, which is the playbook's preferred position, and it preserves the parties' existing payment-gating (now tightened to the undisputed amount of the relevant invoice) rather than expanding our obligations.

The added subsection covers the two remaining gaps the rule requires: Customer Data ownership and an express no-joint-ownership statement, and it carves Company Data / our pre-existing IP out of 'Contractor's Information' so it cannot be swept into Contractor's exclusive property under 4(b).

No assignment of our IP or data to Contractor is created or left in place; Contractor's background IP (4(b)) and the embedded-IP licence-back (4(c)) are expressly left intact, consistent with the rule's allowance for the Vendor keeping its platform and tools.

The failed 'minimal edit' heuristic (ratio 0.844) is explained by the necessary replacement of the vague 'to the extent ... invoiced and paid' ownership test with assignment language; the operative subject and the rest of the sentence are retained, so no smaller edit would reach the playbook position.

Comment is accurate, correctly prefixed, concise and in first person plural; it states what changed, the playbook basis, and confirms Contractor's retained rights are unaffected. Minor residual risk to confirm on turn: that the inserted lettering '(e)' does not collide with an existing subsection and that 'Services' is a defined term in this MSA.

payload.sectionRef: § 3 CONTRACTOR'S COMPENSATION.

paragraphs.text: 3. CONTRACTOR'S COMPENSATION.

(a) During the term of this Agreement, Company agrees to compensate Contractor as set forth in each Statement of Work. Contractor will be compensated on a time and materials. In addition, Company shall reimburse Contractor its actual out-of-pocket expenses as reasonably incurred by Contractor in connection with its performance of the Services as negotiated in each Statement of Work.

(b) Contractor shall bill Company as set forth in the relevant Statement of Work. Each invoice submitted by Contractor will provide supporting detail for the Services invoiced, including, to the extent applicable to a particular engagement, the dates of Services and hours worked at the applicable rate by Statement of Work. Invoices shall also include receipts or other supporting detail concerning related expenses within the billing cycle. Contractor reserves the right to change rates with 30 days notice to Company.

(c) All fees, charges and other amounts payable to Contractor hereunder do not include any sales, use, excise, value added or other applicable taxes, tariffs or duties, payment of which shall be the sole responsibility of Company (excluding any applicable taxes based on Contractor's net income or taxes arising from the independent contractor relationship between Contractor and its personnel). In the event that such taxes, tariffs or duties are assessed against Contractor, Company shall reimburse Contractor for any such amounts paid by Contractor or provide Contractor with valid tax exemption certificates with respect thereto.

input.rationale: The agreement contains no audit, inspection, verification or examination right exercisable by Contractor against Company. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "examine", "records", "usage" and "premises" return no such right: § 3 (Compensation) only requires Contractor to provide invoice supporting detail to us (a Contractor obligation in our favour), § 4 addresses ownership/acceptance of Works with no inspection right, and the only access language (p0007) obliges Contractor to comply with Company's computer system access and security policies — again a restriction on the counterparty, not access to our systems. Because there is no audit right binding the Customer, there is nothing exceeding the AUDIT limits on frequency, notice, cost allocation or system access, and no redline is warranted. Adding an audit framework would only create a right against us that does not currently exist.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The AUDIT rule is a defensive/limiting rule: it caps audit rights that a Vendor holds against us. This agreement grants RadialSpark no such right at all, which is better than the preferred position.

What I checked:
- **§ 3 (Contractor's Compensation)** — the flagged records/invoicing candidate. It runs the other way: Contractor must supply invoice supporting detail, dates, hours and expense receipts *to us*. No reciprocal right for Contractor to examine our books or usage.
- **§ 4 (Ownership/Acceptance)** — ownership of Works, Contractor's Information licence-back, and post-payment modification rights. No inspection or verification right.
- **Full-text sweeps** for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "examine", "records", "usage", "premises", "right to review" — no audit or verification right binding Clear Capital.
- **§ 1, p0007** — the only access-related language obliges Contractor to comply with *our* policies on access to and security of Company computer systems. That is a counterparty restriction operating in our favour, not remote access to our systems, so it is not flagged.

No edit made, per the principle of not creating a Vendor right that the current bargain omits. If RadialSpark later proposes an audit or usage-verification clause (e.g., in a Statement of Work), the playbook position should be applied then: once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, Contractor-borne cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct access to our systems.

paragraphs.text: 4. OWNERSHIP OF MATERIALS RELATED TO SERVICES; ACCEPTANCE.

(a) The parties agree that all drawings, documents, designs, models, inventions, computer programs, computer systems, data, computer documentation and other tangible materials authored or prepared by Contractor for Company as the work product required by a Statement of Work (collectively, the "Works"), are the property of Company to the extent that such Works were created by Contractor for Company over a time period for which Company has been invoiced and said invoice has been paid. Contractor agrees to render, at Company's sole cost
and expense, all reasonably required assistance to Company to protect the rights herein above described, including executing other documents as requested by Company.

(b) Company acknowledges that Contractor provides consulting and development services to other clients, and agrees that nothing in this Agreement shall be deemed or construed to prevent Contractor from delivering on such business. In particular, Company agrees that, notwithstanding anything to the contrary set forth herein:

(i) as part of Contractor's provision of the Services hereunder, Contractor may utilize its own proprietary works of authorship, that have not been created specifically for Company, including without limitation software, methodologies, tools, specifications, drawings, sketches, models, samples, records and documentation, as well as copyrights, trademarks, servicemarks, ideas, concepts, know-how, techniques, knowledge or data, which have been originated, developed or purchased by Contractor or by third parties under contract to Contractor, and, (ii) Contractor's Information and Contractor's administrative communications and records relating to the Services shall not be deemed to be Works and are and shall remain the sole and exclusive property of Contractor and Company shall not resell or make use of said property in any other manner other than in connection with the software Company receives under this Agreement.

(c) To the extent that Contractor incorporates any of Contractor's Information into the Works, Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.

(d) Consultant agrees that after Company pays Contractor in full, or after the termination of this agreement, Company may make any changes or additions to the software Consultant created for Company under this Agreement, which Company in Company's discretion may consider necessary, and Company may engage others to make any such changes or additions, without further payments to Consultant.

Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.

No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.

Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).

Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.

Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

The residual deviation is correctly identified and in-scope for this parametric rule, which expressly covers 'price uplift language' and requires ongoing pricing predictability: § 3(b) (p0014) gives Contractor a unilateral, uncapped, unlimited-frequency right to raise rates on 30 days' notice, which is the only pricing-uplift lever in an evergreen deal.

Redline is directionally correct for the customer and additive rather than destructive: it preserves the existing 30-day notice bargain and appends only the playbook cap (once per 12 months; lesser of CPI and 3%) plus a fix of rates in already-executed Statements of Work. The SOW rate-fix is well-targeted to the actual exposure, since the § 6(a) convenience exit is only available when no Statement of Work is outstanding, leaving Company unable to escape a mid-SOW increase.

payload.sectionRef: § 1 PURPOSE OF ENGAGEMENT.

paragraphs.text: 1. PURPOSE OF ENGAGEMENT.

(a) Company agrees to retain Contractor to perform the consulting services for Company, on a task by task basis (the "Services"), and Contractor agrees to furnish the Services on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in this Agreement. During the term of this Agreement, Company and Contractor will develop and agree upon statements of work defining the Services and work product to be provided by Contractor, Contractor's compensation, additional terms and conditions, if any, applicable to a particular engagement and such other details as the parties deem appropriate (each a "Statement of Work"). A Statement of Work may provide specifications for deliverables to be provided thereunder (the "Specifications"). Statements of Work that are from time to time agreed upon shall reference this Agreement, and shall be executed by the parties and attached hereto and shall form a part hereof. In all instances of a conflict, between the provisions of this Agreement and the specific provisions set forth in a Statement of Work, the provisions of this Agreement shall control.

(b) Contractor shall provide sufficient qualified personnel to perform the Services in a professional and workmanlike manner in accordance with industry standards. A Statement of Work may designate certain individuals as "Key Personnel" for an engagement, and the parties subsequently may agree in writing that additional individuals are Key Personnel for such engagement. If there are Key Personnel for an engagement, Contractor shall provide the Services through those personnel and such additional personnel of Contractor as Contractor may from time to time determine to be required for the performance of the Services. Company shall have the right to interview and approve such additional personnel at Company's request. If one or more Key Personnel terminate their employment with Contractor or otherwise become

unavailable to work on an engagement for reasons beyond Contractor's reasonable control, Contractor may provide the Services through other personnel with comparable training and experience. If Company becomes dissatisfied with any of Contractor's personnel providing the Services, Company may notify Contractor of the details of its dissatisfaction, and the parties shall cooperate to remedy the problem as soon as possible. If Company reasonably requests, Contractor shall reassign the individual who is the subject of Company's dissatisfaction and replace that person with other personnel in accordance with this Agreement.

(c) Unless otherwise provided in a Statement of Work, Contractor shall provide the Services at Contractor's facility. Contractor shall provide computing equipment consistent with the Services to be provided under the Statement of Work. When services are provided at a Company facility, Company shall provide workspace and other facilities such as computer support consistent with the requirements of the Services to be provided under the Statement of Work. Contractor shall cause its personnel at Company's facility to comply with Company's (i) safety and security rules and other rules applicable to those working in the facility, and (ii) Company's policies concerning access to and security of any Company computer system to which Contractor may have access; provided, that Company has provided Contractor with copies of such rules and policies or has advised Contractor of the existence of such rules and policies.

(d) Company may request changes that affect the scope or duration of the Services relating to any Statement of Work, including changes in the Specifications and changes in the deliverables to be delivered. Company acknowledges that any change in Specifications may result in changes to estimated fees and estimated timeline for creation of deliverables. Company also may request a change in the Schedule without changing the scope of the Services relating to the applicable Statement of Work. In either case, the parties shall negotiate in good faith a reasonable and equitable adjustment in the applicable fees, Schedule and Specifications. Contractor shall continue work pursuant to the existing Statement of Work, and shall not be bound by any change requested by Company, until such change has been accepted in writing by Contractor.

(e) The obligations of Company in connection with a particular engagement shall be set forth in the applicable Statement of Work. Company agrees to perform such obligations in accordance with, and subject to, such Statement of Work. Company acknowledges that when a Statement of Work provides that Company's personnel are to work with Contractor's personnel in connection with an engagement, Company's failure to assign Company personnel having skills commensurate with their role with respect to such engagement could adversely affect Contractor's ability to provide the Services.

(f) To the extent Contractor provides any third party materials and products Contractor acknowledges that it shall be solely responsible for ensuring the functionality and specifications of such third party materials and products used in performing Services under this Agreement.
2. TERM. The term of this Agreement shall begin on the date hereof and shall continue until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6 hereof.

payload.sectionRef: § 6 TERMINATION.

paragraphs.text: 6. TERMINATION.
(a) At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, either party may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon fifteen (15) days advance notice to the other.

(b) In addition, either party may terminate this Agreement or any outstanding Statement of Work, upon fifteen (15) days written notice to the other party, in the event such other party breaches a material term of this Agreement or any Statement of Work and such breach remains uncured at the end of such fifteen (15) day period. Upon any such termination, Contractor will be paid all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned in connection with the performance of the Services through the effective date of such termination. Contractor shall provide to Company, and hereby assigns to Company, all right, title and interest to any Works in progress.

Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing

Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

payload.sectionRef: § 1 PURPOSE OF ENGAGEMENT.

paragraphs.text: 1. PURPOSE OF ENGAGEMENT.

(a) Company agrees to retain Contractor to perform the consulting services for Company, on a task by task basis (the "Services"), and Contractor agrees to furnish the Services on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in this Agreement. During the term of this Agreement, Company and Contractor will develop and agree upon statements of work defining the Services and work product to be provided by Contractor, Contractor's compensation, additional terms and conditions, if any, applicable to a particular engagement and such other details as the parties deem appropriate (each a "Statement of Work"). A Statement of Work may provide specifications for deliverables to be provided thereunder (the "Specifications"). Statements of Work that are from time to time agreed upon shall reference this Agreement, and shall be executed by the parties and attached hereto and shall form a part hereof. In all instances of a conflict, between the provisions of this Agreement and the specific provisions set forth in a Statement of Work, the provisions of this Agreement shall control.

(b) Contractor shall provide sufficient qualified personnel to perform the Services in a professional and workmanlike manner in accordance with industry standards. A Statement of Work may designate certain individuals as "Key Personnel" for an engagement, and the parties subsequently may agree in writing that additional individuals are Key Personnel for such engagement. If there are Key Personnel for an engagement, Contractor shall provide the Services through those personnel and such additional personnel of Contractor as Contractor may from time to time determine to be required for the performance of the Services. Company shall have the right to interview and approve such additional personnel at Company's request. If one or more Key Personnel terminate their employment with Contractor or otherwise become

unavailable to work on an engagement for reasons beyond Contractor's reasonable control, Contractor may provide the Services through other personnel with comparable training and experience. If Company becomes dissatisfied with any of Contractor's personnel providing the Services, Company may notify Contractor of the details of its dissatisfaction, and the parties shall cooperate to remedy the problem as soon as possible. If Company reasonably requests, Contractor shall reassign the individual who is the subject of Company's dissatisfaction and replace that person with other personnel in accordance with this Agreement.

(c) Unless otherwise provided in a Statement of Work, Contractor shall provide the Services at Contractor's facility. Contractor shall provide computing equipment consistent with the Services to be provided under the Statement of Work. When services are provided at a Company facility, Company shall provide workspace and other facilities such as computer support consistent with the requirements of the Services to be provided under the Statement of Work. Contractor shall cause its personnel at Company's facility to comply with Company's (i) safety and security rules and other rules applicable to those working in the facility, and (ii) Company's policies concerning access to and security of any Company computer system to which Contractor may have access; provided, that Company has provided Contractor with copies of such rules and policies or has advised Contractor of the existence of such rules and policies.

(d) Company may request changes that affect the scope or duration of the Services relating to any Statement of Work, including changes in the Specifications and changes in the deliverables to be delivered. Company acknowledges that any change in Specifications may result in changes to estimated fees and estimated timeline for creation of deliverables. Company also may request a change in the Schedule without changing the scope of the Services relating to the applicable Statement of Work. In either case, the parties shall negotiate in good faith a reasonable and equitable adjustment in the applicable fees, Schedule and Specifications. Contractor shall continue work pursuant to the existing Statement of Work, and shall not be bound by any change requested by Company, until such change has been accepted in writing by Contractor.

(e) The obligations of Company in connection with a particular engagement shall be set forth in the applicable Statement of Work. Company agrees to perform such obligations in accordance with, and subject to, such Statement of Work. Company acknowledges that when a Statement of Work provides that Company's personnel are to work with Contractor's personnel in connection with an engagement, Company's failure to assign Company personnel having skills commensurate with their role with respect to such engagement could adversely affect Contractor's ability to provide the Services.

(f) To the extent Contractor provides any third party materials and products Contractor acknowledges that it shall be solely responsible for ensuring the functionality and specifications of such third party materials and products used in performing Services under this Agreement.
2. TERM. The term of this Agreement shall begin on the date hereof and shall continue until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6 hereof.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 5 warrants only legality of performance, authority/rights and non-infringement; there is no warranty that the Services or Works will conform to the Specifications, no warranty period, no malicious-code warranty and no repair/replace/re-perform/refund remedy. The professional-and-workmanlike standard in Paragraph 1(b) is a performance covenant only, and Paragraph 5(e) disclaims all implied warranties (including merchantability and fitness), leaving Clear Capital with no conformance protection. Added a new Paragraph 5(f) with a 12-month deliverable/software and 90-day services conformance warranty, no-malicious-code warranty, express remedy at Contractor's option, and a carve-out from the disclaimer; fallback is 90/30 days with the same remedies.

Original paragraphs:
p0024: (a) Contractor represents and warrants to Company that Contractor's performance of the Services called for by this Agreement, to its knowledge, does not and shall not violate any applicable law, rule, or regulation;
p0030: (e) THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES IN THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE IN LIEU OF ALL OTHER WARRANTIES, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING THE IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.
p0005: (b) Contractor shall provide sufficient qualified personnel to perform the Services in a professional and workmanlike manner in accordance with industry standards. A Statement of Work may designate certain individuals as "Key Personnel" for an engagement, and the parties subsequently may agree in writing that additional individuals are Key Personnel for such engagement. I have what I need. The agreement is engagement-by-engagement with no volume or spend commitment:

- **§1(a)/(b)**: Services are retained "on a task by task basis," defined only through mutually agreed Statements of Work.
- **§3(a)/(b)**: Compensation is "on a time and materials" basis "as set forth in each Statement of Work" — no retainer, minimum hours, or guaranteed spend.
- **§6(b)**: On termination, Contractor is paid only "all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned... through the effective date" — a true-up, not a shortfall penalty or acceleration.

Searches for "minimum," "commit," "shortfall," "take or pay," "retainer," "non-refundable," and "prepaid" returned no commitment language anywhere in the document. No volume caps on our usage either. This meets the preferred position, so no redline is warranted.

input.quote: (a) During the term of this Agreement, Company agrees to compensate Contractor as set forth in each Statement of Work. Contractor will be compensated on a time and materials.
input.rationale: No minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall charge, or volume restriction on Customer appears in the Agreement. Services are engaged "on a task by task basis" under mutually agreed Statements of Work (§1(a)), and compensation is strictly time-and-materials plus reimbursed expenses as set forth in each SOW (§3(a)-(b)), so fees are payable only for services actually ordered and performed. Targeted searches for "minimum," "commit," "shortfall," "take or pay," "retainer," "non-refundable," and "prepaid" returned no commitment language. On termination, §6(b) entitles Contractor only to "all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned... through the effective date of such termination" — an incurred-cost true-up rather than a penalty or accelerated commitment. Section 3 also contains no minimum hours or guaranteed spend. This satisfies the preferred position, so no redline is proposed. (Noted but out of scope for this rule: §6(a) permits convenience termination only when no uncompleted SOW is outstanding, which is a term/exit point rather than a purchase commitment.)

Targeted searches for "minimum," "commit," "shortfall," "take or pay," "retainer," "non-refundable," and "prepaid" returned no commitment language. On termination, §6(b) entitles Contractor only to "all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned... through the effective date of such termination" — an incurred-cost true-up rather than a penalty or accelerated commitment. Section 3 also contains no minimum hours or guaranteed spend. This satisfies the preferred position, so no redline is proposed. (Noted but out of scope for this rule: §6(a) permits convenience termination only when no uncompleted SOW is outstanding, which is a term/exit point rather than a purchase commitment.)

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

Parties: we represent Clear Capital; counterparty is RadialSpark, LLC.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The AUDIT rule is a defensive/limiting rule: it caps audit rights that a Vendor holds against us. This agreement grants RadialSpark no such right at all, which is better than the preferred position.

What I checked:
- **§ 3 (Contractor's Compensation)** — the flagged records/invoicing candidate. It runs the other way: Contractor must supply invoice supporting detail, dates, hours and expense receipts *to us*. No reciprocal right for Contractor to examine our books or usage.
- **§ 4 (Ownership/Acceptance)** — ownership of Works, Contractor's Information licence-back, and post-payment modification rights. No inspection or verification right.
- **Full-text sweeps** for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "examine", "records", "usage", "premises", "right to review" — no audit or verification right binding Clear Capital.
- **§ 1, p0007** — the only access-related language obliges Contractor to comply with *our* policies on access to and security of Company computer systems. That is a counterparty restriction operating in our favour, not remote access to our systems, so it is not flagged.

No edit made, per the principle of not creating a Vendor right that the current bargain omits. If RadialSpark later proposes an audit or usage-verification clause (e.g., in a Statement of Work), the playbook position should be applied then: once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, Contractor-borne cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct access to our systems.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline needed.

The Agreement contains no take-or-pay exposure for Clear Capital. Work is engaged task-by-task under Statements of Work, compensation is time-and-materials only, and termination triggers payment solely for fees already incurred or earned — an incurred-cost true-up rather than a shortfall penalty. This meets our preferred position, so I proposed no changes.

One adjacent item I noted for the record but did not flag under this rule: §6(a) allows convenience termination only when no uncompleted Statement of Work is outstanding. That is an exit/term issue rather than a minimum purchase commitment, and it would be better addressed under whichever playbook rule governs termination rights.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
No minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall charge, or volume restriction on Customer appears in the Agreement. Services are engaged "on a task by task basis" under mutually agreed Statements of Work (§1(a)), and compensation is strictly time-and-materials plus reimbursed expenses as set forth in each SOW (§3(a)-(b)), so fees are payable only for services actually ordered and performed. Targeted searches for "minimum," "commit," "shortfall," "take or pay," "retainer," "non-refundable," and "prepaid" returned no commitment language. On termination, §6(b) entitles Contractor only to "all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned... through the effective date of such termination" — an incurred-cost true-up rather than a penalty or accelerated commitment. Section 3 also contains no minimum hours or guaranteed spend. This satisfies the preferred position, so no redline is proposed. (Noted but out of scope for this rule: §6(a) permits convenience termination only when no uncompleted SOW is outstanding, which is a term/exit point rather than a purchase commitment.)

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

**Finding: missing (deviation by omission) — TRANSITION**

The termination section (§ 6) is silent on exit mechanics. It covers only the 15-day notice rights, payment of Contractor's accrued fees, and assignment of Works in progress. Document-wide searches for "transition," "return," and "delet" returned nothing, and the confidentiality provision (§ 8, p0038–p0040) restricts use and disclosure but imposes no return or destruction duty. Section 4 gives us ownership of Works but no delivery-back mechanism.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** new § 6(c) after p0033 requiring RadialSpark to (i) provide up to six (6) months of transition assistance at then-current rates on request, (ii) return all Works, Company data and Confidential Information within thirty (30) days in a commonly used machine-readable format, and (iii) thereafter delete and certify deletion in writing. Language is adapted to this Agreement's defined terms (Company, Contractor, Works, Confidential Information) because "Customer Data" is not defined here. Fallback of 90 days' assistance is flagged in the comment.

Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
Section 6 addresses only notice periods, payment of Contractor's accrued fees and assignment of Works in progress. Searches for "transition", "return" and "delet" return no results, and the confidentiality provision (p0038-p0040) imposes only use/disclosure restrictions with no return or destruction obligation. Accordingly there is no post-termination transition assistance, no obligation to return Company data, Works or Confidential Information in a usable format, and no deletion/certification requirement — a medium-severity gap under TRANSITION. We insert a new § 6(c) tracking the model language (six months' assistance at Contractor's then-current rates, return within 30 days in machine-readable format, then certified deletion), using this Agreement's defined terms (Company, Contractor, Works, Confidential Information) since "Customer Data" is not defined here.

Original paragraphs:
p0032: (a) At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, either party may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon fifteen (15) days advance notice to the other.
p0033: (b) In addition, either party may terminate this Agreement or any outstanding Statement of Work, upon fifteen (15) days written notice to the other party, in the event such other party breaches a material term of this Agreement or any Statement of Work and such breach remains uncured at the end of such fifteen (15) day period. Upon any such termination, Contractor will be paid all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned in connection with the performance of the Services through the effective date of such termination. Contractor shall provide to Company, and hereby assigns to Company, all right, title and interest to any Works in progress.

During the term of this Agreement, Company and Contractor will develop and agree upon statements of work defining the Services and work product to be provided by Contractor, Contractor's compensation, additional terms and conditions, if any, applicable to a particular engagement and such other details as the parties deem appropriate (each a "Statement of Work"). Statements of Work that are from time to time agreed upon shall reference this Agreement, and shall be executed by the parties and attached hereto and shall form a part hereof. p0033: (b) In addition, either party may terminate this Agreement or any outstanding Statement of Work, upon fifteen (15) days written notice to the other party, in the event such other party breaches a material term of this Agreement or any Statement of Work and such breach remains uncured at the end of such fifteen (15) day period. input.quote: Contractor shall bill Company as set forth in the relevant Statement of Work. Each invoice submitted by Contractor will provide supporting detail for the Services invoiced, including, to the extent applicable to a particular engagement, the dates of Services and hours worked at the applicable rate by Statement of Work.
input.rationale: No audit, inspection, verification or monitoring right runs against Clear Capital anywhere in the agreement. A document-wide regex sweep for "audit|inspect|verif|examin|monitor|books and records|compliance review" returns zero matches, and the sections flagged by the planner contain no such right: § 3 governs compensation and invoicing, § 4 governs ownership and acceptance of Works. Both candidate paragraphs run in our favour rather than against us: p0014 (§ 3) obliges Contractor to supply invoice supporting detail, dates, hours worked and expense receipts to us, and p0007(ii) (§ 1) requires Contractor to observe Company's rules on access to and security of Company computer systems — a restriction on the counterparty, not a grant of access to our systems. Because AUDIT constrains a Vendor-favourable right and no such right exists here, there is nothing exceeding the limits on frequency, notice, cost allocation or system access, so no redline or comment is warranted. Inserting frequency/notice/cost limits would gratuitously create a Vendor audit right that the current bargain omits, contrary to the minimal-edit principle. The failed deterministic check "audit frequency limited" is a false signal: the regex cannot match a frequency cap because there is no audit clause to cap, and the apparent frequency hits are incidental substrings inside ordinary words ("concerning", "concepts"). Residual risk to monitor: a future Statement of Work could introduce an audit or usage-verification right, in which case the preferred position applies — once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor bound by confidentiality, Contractor-borne cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct access to our systems.

Finding submitted. Summary of what I found and did:

**The planner hint was wrong.** It predicted no insurance clause existed (`likelyAbsent: true`) and suggested inserting one near sec-5. In fact, Section 14 insurance sits at **p0048**, buried inside sec-7 ("Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor") — the outline headings hid it. So this is a **deviation** (amend existing limits), not a **missing** finding requiring insertion.

**What already complies:**
- Workers' compensation as required by statute ✓
- Certificates of insurance on Company request, plus notice of material change ✓

**Three gaps against the preferred position:**
1. **CGL** — flat USD 1,000,000 with no per-occurrence/aggregate structure; preferred is 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate.
2. **E&O** — USD 1,000,000, which only reaches our *fallback*, not the preferred USD 2,000,000.
3. **Cyber/privacy** — entirely absent.

**Why cyber is clearly triggered** (I verified rather than assumed, since the rule conditions it on data processing):
- p0038 defines Confidential Information to include Company "documents, software, reports, data, records" and Company records and information obtained by Contractor.
- p0007 has Contractor personnel working at Company facilities and accessing Company computer systems under Company security policies.

That data-plus-premises-plus-systems profile is exactly the risk the rule targets, and a vendor in that position with zero cyber cover edges toward the stated walk-away.

**The redline** is deliberately surgical — a single in-place replacement that preserves the existing sentence structure, workers' comp, certificates and notice language, while adding the 2M CGL aggregate, raising E&O to 2M, and adding 5M cyber conditioned on Contractor processing or accessing Company data. I omitted the model language's one-year tail because the preferred position statement doesn't require it, keeping the edit proportionate. The comment offers the documented fallback (2M cyber, E&O at 1M) as a negotiating path.

One item I noted but did not redline, flagging it for your judgment: the certificate provision accepts evidence of **"self-insurance"**, which could let RadialSpark satisfy these limits off its own balance sheet rather than through a rated carrier. That partly undercuts the value of the limits we just raised. It falls outside this rule's scope, so I left it alone, but it may be worth a separate ask if RadialSpark is not of substantial size.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Contrary to the planner hint that no insurance clause exists, Section 14 (p0048, located in sec-7) does contain vendor insurance and already satisfies two elements of the preferred position: workers' compensation as required by statute and certificates of insurance on Company request. Three gaps remain. (1) Commercial general liability is stated as a flat USD 1,000,000 with no per-occurrence/aggregate structure, short of the preferred USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate. (2) Professional errors and omissions cover is USD 1,000,000, which only meets the fallback rather than the preferred USD 2,000,000. (3) There is no cyber/privacy liability cover at all. Cyber cover is squarely triggered here: under p0038 Contractor obtains Company "documents, software, reports, data, records" and Company records and information as Confidential Information, and under p0007 Contractor personnel work at Company facilities and have access to Company computer systems subject to Company security policies. That combination of data processing plus premises and systems access is exactly the risk profile the rule targets, and a vendor processing our data with zero cyber cover approaches the walk-away position. Because a clause exists but falls short, this is a deviation cured by amending the limits in place rather than inserting a new paragraph. The redline is surgical: it keeps the existing sentence structure, workers' compensation, certificates and notice-of-change language untouched, adds the USD 2M CGL aggregate, raises E&O to USD 2M, and adds USD 5M cyber and privacy liability conditioned on Contractor processing or accessing Company data or Confidential Information. The one-year tail from the model language was omitted to keep the edit minimal, as the preferred position statement does not require it. The comment offers the documented fallback of USD 2M cyber with E&O held at USD 1M.

Original paragraphs:
p0048: 14. INSURANCE. Throughout the term of this Agreement, Contractor shall maintain workers compensation insurance in the amount required by statute, comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) and professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000), in connection with the provision of Services by Contractor pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. At Company's request, Contractor shall provide Company with certificates or other acceptable evidence of insurance or self-insurance evidencing the above coverage and shall provide Company with prompt written notice of any material change.

Resolved definitions:
Agreement: THIS MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT ("Agreement"), dated as of 09/24/2018 (the "Effective Date"), is between Clear Capital (the "Company") and RadialSpark, LLC (the "Contractor"). WHEREAS, Company desires from time to time to retain Contractor to perform certain management consulting services for Company; and WHEREAS, Contractor desires to perform such management consulting services for Company; NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the foregoing premises, and the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, the parties hereto agree as follows:
Contractor: THIS MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT ("Agreement"), dated as of 09/24/2018 (the "Effective Date"), is between Clear Capital (the "Company") and RadialSpark, LLC (the "Contractor"). WHEREAS, Company desires from time to time to retain Contractor to perform certain management consulting services for Company; and WHEREAS, Contractor desires to perform such management consulting services for Company; NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the foregoing premises, and the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, the parties hereto agree as follows:
Services: (a) Company agrees to retain Contractor to perform the consulting services for Company, on a task by task basis (the "Services"), and Contractor agrees to furnish the Services on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in this Agreement. During the term of this Agreement, Company and Contractor will develop and agree upon statements of work defining the Services and work product to be provided by Contractor, Contractor's compensation, additional terms and conditions, if any, applicable to a particular engagement and such other details as the parties deem appropriate (each a "Statement of Work"). A Statement of Work may provide specifications for deliverables to be provided thereunder (the "Specifications"). Statements of Work that are from time to time agreed upon shall reference this Agreement, and shall be executed by the parties and attached hereto and shall form a part hereof. In all instances of a conflict, between the provisions of this Agreement and the specific provisions set forth in a Statement of Work, the provisions of this Agreement shall control.

Rendered redline:
p0048: 14. INSURANCE. Throughout the term of this Agreement, Contractor shall maintain workers compensation insurance in the amount required by statute, comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) per occurrence and two million dollars ($2,000,000) in the aggregate, professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least two million dollars ($2,000,000), and, where Contractor processes, stores or has access to Company data or Confidential Information, cyber and privacy liability insurance with coverage of at least five million dollars ($5,000,000), in connection with the provision of Services by Contractor pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. At Company's request, Contractor shall provide Company with certificates or other acceptable evidence of insurance or self-insurance evidencing the above coverage and shall provide Company with prompt written notice of any material change.

[Playbook] Section 14 already covers workers' compensation and certificates, but the limits fall short and there is no cyber cover even though Contractor handles Company data and accesses our systems and facilities, so we added a USD 2M general liability aggregate, raised errors and omissions cover to USD 2M, and added USD 5M cyber and privacy liability. If USD 5M is not available, we can accept USD 2M cyber liability with errors and omissions held at USD 1M.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — RadialSpark Services Agreement (Clear Capital)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** Legal 
**Re:** Playbook review — verified findings and negotiation positions 
**Party posture:** We act for Clear Capital (Company / Customer). RadialSpark is Contractor (Vendor).

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and recorded nineteen findings. Eight items are compliant or benign and need no redline (exclusivity, liquidated damages, non-compete, MFN, minimum commitments, and the renewal-mechanics limbs of the term provisions). The commercial risk is concentrated in three critical items: (i) there is **no Vendor indemnity anywhere in the document** — Section 7 is captioned "INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR" but contains only liability limitations, and a document-wide search for "indemn" and "hold harmless" returns nothing, leaving Contractor's Section 5(c) non-infringement warranty unbacked by any defence obligation; (ii) Section 7(a) caps Contractor's liability at fees actually paid under the particular Statement of Work, with no 12-month measure, no floor, and no effective carve-outs (the only carve-out cross-references Paragraph 9, the Independent Contractor clause); and (iii) Section 4(a) declares the Works to be Company property but contains **no present assignment** of IP and is silent on Company Data and our pre-existing IP, while Section 4(b) sweeps broadly defined Contractor materials, records and "data" into Contractor's exclusive property.

Secondary but material: we have no convenience exit while any Statement of Work is open (Section 6(a)), yet Contractor may exit on fifteen days' notice; Section 3(b) gives Contractor a unilateral, uncapped right to change rates on 30 days' notice with no ability for us to walk away mid-SOW; Section 10 blocks routine affiliate/successor assignment; there is no conformance warranty (Section 5 warrants only legality, authority and non-infringement, and Section 5(e) disclaims implied warranties); there is no post-termination transition, data return or deletion obligation; Section 14 insurance omits cyber/privacy cover entirely despite Contractor holding our data and accessing our systems; and Section 11/19 select Arizona law and mandatory arbitration.

One finding (AUDIT) failed verification and is carried below for information only; we do not rely on it and do not propose a redline against it.

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Position / proposal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 7 (Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor) | Insert Contractor indemnity (IP infringement, breach of law, Confidential Information breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) as new § 7(d), carved out of the liability cap, with notice/control/cooperation mechanics. No Company-side indemnity exists, so none needs narrowing. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 4 (Ownership of Materials Related to Services; Acceptance) | Add a present, irrevocable assignment of the Works (still tied to payment of the applicable undisputed invoice) and a new § 4(e) confirming we retain all rights in Company Data and our pre-existing IP, with no joint ownership. Contractor background IP (4(b)) and the licence-back (4(c)) already meet the playbook. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 7 | Make the cap mutual at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; add uncapped Excluded Claims; confirm fees due are not subject to the cap. § 7(b) consequential waiver is acceptable. **Fallback:** mutual 12-month fees cap with carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 7 (clause reviewed: § 10 Nonassignability) | Add Company affiliate/successor carve-out, bar Contractor assignment to our competitors, and confirm a Company change of control is not an assignment and triggers no Contractor exit or re-pricing right. |
| 5 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 6 (Termination) | Add a Company 30-day convenience right over the Agreement or any SOW (in whole or part) with refund of prepaid fees and no penalty or acceleration; confine Contractor's convenience right to 90 days' notice when no SOW is open. **Fallback:** 60 days for us. |
| 6 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 4 | Extend the § 4(c) background-IP licence to our Affiliates and contractors (control-based definition, as "Affiliates" is undefined), add "irrevocable", and carve the licence out of § 10 for transfer to a successor. Not a walk-away item, as the licence is not expressly revocable. |
| 7 | High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | § 1 (Purpose of Engagement) | No exclusivity or sole-supplier undertaking; task-by-task SOW model with no requirements or volume commitment. No redline. |
| 8 | High | LD — Liquidated damages/penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 6 | No liquidated damages, penalty or early-termination fee; § 6(b) and § 7(c) limit our post-termination exposure to fees and expenses incurred or earned to the termination date. No redline. |
| 9 | High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | § 4 | No non-compete, field-of-use, territory or exclusivity restraint on us; § 4(b) is a licence-scope limit and § 13 is a mutual personnel non-solicit. No redline. |
| 10 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal / pricing predictability | Deviation | § 3 (Contractor's Compensation) | Renewal mechanics are fine (evergreen term, 15-day exit, no auto-renewal). Cap the § 3(b) unilateral rate increase: once per 12 months, lesser of CPI and 3%, with rates in an executed SOW fixed for its duration. **Fallback:** 5% cap. |
| 11 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | Deviation | § 5 (Representations and Warranties; Disclaimer) | Add new § 5(f): 12-month deliverable/software and 90-day services conformance warranty, no-malicious-code warranty, express repair/replace/re-perform/refund remedy, carved out of the § 5(e) disclaimer. **Fallback:** 90/30 days, same remedies. |
| 12 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 6 | Insert § 6(c): six months' transition assistance at Contractor's then-current rates, return of Company data, Works and Confidential Information within 30 days in machine-readable format, then certified deletion. |
| 13 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 7 (clauses reviewed: §§ 11, 19) | Replace Arizona law with New York law and replace mandatory arbitration with exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County. Arbitration is domestic, so medium rather than walk-away. |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 7 (clause reviewed: § 13) | § 13 is already close to our fallback (mutual, one year, Services personnel, solicitation only). Add general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs rather than deleting. |
| 15 | Medium | MFN | Compliant | § 3 | No MFN burdening us; the only pricing lever runs the other way (§ 3(b) rate change right, addressed at item 10). No redline. |
| 16 | Medium | MINCOMMIT | Compliant | § 1 | No minimum purchase, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume restriction; strict time-and-materials under §§ 1(a) and 3(a)-(b). No redline. |
| 17 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Needs review (**verification failed**) | § 3 | No audit, inspection or verification right runs against us; the deterministic "audit frequency limited" check failed because there is no audit clause to cap. No redline (inserting limits would gratuitously create a Vendor audit right). Monitor: a future SOW could introduce one. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Deviation | § 7 (clause reviewed: § 14) | § 14 already covers workers' compensation and certificates. Amend limits in place: add USD 2M CGL aggregate, raise E&O to USD 2M, and add USD 5M cyber/privacy cover conditioned on Contractor processing or accessing Company data or Confidential Information. **Fallback:** USD 2M cyber with E&O held at USD 1M. |

## Walk-away items

No finding is recorded as meeting a walk-away threshold, and two findings expressly state they fall short of one (GOVLAW: arbitration is domestic rather than seated abroad; LICENSE: the licence is not expressly revocable at Contractor's discretion). The following are the closest to that line and should be treated as non-negotiable in substance:

1. **No Vendor indemnity plus a fees-paid cap (items 1 and 3).** The combination of no indemnity anywhere in the document, a per-SOW "fees actually paid" cap, no effective carve-outs, and the § 7(c) attorneys' fees waiver leaves us with no meaningful remedy. Both must move together.
2. **No present assignment of the Works and no Company Data provision (item 2).** Rights in work product we fund are unallocated and potentially Contractor-owned, and § 4(b) sweeps broadly defined Contractor materials, records and "data" into Contractor's exclusive property.
3. **Zero cyber/privacy insurance (item 18).** Per the finding, a vendor processing our data with no cyber cover "approaches the walk-away position": under § 14 there is none, while § 38 confidentiality and § 1(b) premises/systems access mean Contractor holds our documents, software, reports, data and records and works on our systems.

## Next steps

1. Issue the redline with the eleven proposed edits (items 1–6, 10–14, 18). Confirm no changes to the eight compliant/benign items so the counterparty sees the edit set is targeted.
2. Lead the negotiation with items 1–3 as a package and hold the stated fallbacks in reserve (LOL-CAP: mutual 12-month cap with the four carve-outs; T4C: 60 days; WARRANTY: 90/30; RENEWAL: 5%; INSURANCE: USD 2M cyber).
3. Confirm with the business the acceptable floor on the § 3(b) rate-increase cap and on transition assistance duration/rates before we trade.
4. Re-run verification on the AUDIT finding, or accept it as a no-action item on the record that no audit right against us exists; either way, flag to the SOW owners that any future SOW introducing audit or usage-verification rights must come back to us (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, Contractor-borne cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct access to our systems).
5. Confirm the Section 7 caption is corrected and the § 7(a) cross-reference to "Paragraph 9" is repointed to the new indemnity, so the carve-out is operative."}
